examples.en: You think you can win with skills like yours?

examples.ko: 네까짓 놈은 상대도 안 된다고 악당이 말해요.
examples.en: The villain says a guy like you is no match for him.

examples.ko: 네까짓 돈 따위는 필요 없다고 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: I shouted that I don't need a measly bit of money like yours.

examples.ko: 네까짓 말에 내가 흔들릴 것 같아요?
examples.en: Do you think I'd be shaken by words from the likes of you?

examples.ko: 네까짓 게 뭘 안다고 큰소리를 치냐고 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: He got angry and asked what someone like you knows to talk so big.

examples.ko: 네까짓 것쯤은 혼자서도 이길 수 있다고 큰소리쳤어요.
examples.en: He boasted that he could beat the likes of you all by himself.

explain: 상대를 아주 낮춰 보는 무례한 말이라 싸울 때나 드라마 대사에서 주로 들려요. 윗사람에게는 절대 쓰면 안 돼요. 보통 '네까짓 게', '네까짓 놈'처럼 뒤에 '것, 게, 놈' 같은 말이 붙어요.
explain_en: This is a very rude way of looking down on someone, so you mostly hear it in fights or drama lines. Never use it to someone older or higher in status. It usually comes before words like '것', '게' or '놈', as in '네까짓 게'.

examples.en: After lunch my whole body feels drowsy and heavy.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 물에 목욕했더니 몸이 노곤해져서 바로 잠들었어요.
examples.en: I took a warm bath, felt languid, and fell asleep right away.

examples.ko: 오후만 되면 노곤한 기분이 들어서 커피를 마셔요.
examples.en: Every afternoon I feel sluggish, so I drink coffee.

examples.ko: 운동을 오래 했더니 노곤하긴 해도 기분은 좋아요.
examples.en: I exercised for a long time, and I'm worn out but feel good.

examples.ko: 봄볕 아래에 앉아 있으니 노곤하고 졸려요.
examples.en: Sitting in the spring sun makes me drowsy and limp.

examples.ko: 여행 첫날은 노곤했지만 설레서 잠이 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I was worn out on the first day of the trip, but I was too excited to sleep.

explain: '피곤하다'가 힘들고 지친 느낌이라면 '노곤하다'는 힘이 쭉 풀려서 나른하고 졸린 느낌이에요. 밥을 먹은 뒤나 목욕, 운동 뒤처럼 기분 좋은 피로에도 잘 어울려요. '나른하다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '피곤하다' means tired and drained, while '노곤하다' is the limp, drowsy feeling when your strength melts away. It fits well after a meal, a bath or exercise, including a pleasant kind of tiredness. It can be used much like '나른하다'.

en: make undisguised; veil; open; be outspoken

examples.ko: 두 나라가 서로 갈등을 노골화하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries are openly showing their conflict with each other.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 요즘 직원을 줄이려는 뜻을 노골화했어요.
examples.en: That company has recently stopped hiding its wish to cut staff.

examples.ko: 후보들이 상대 비판을 노골화하면서 분위기가 험악해졌어요.
examples.en: As the candidates openly attacked each other, the mood turned nasty.
He makes his dissatisfaction with me plain for everyone to see.
I held back my words so as not to bring the conflict into the open.

examples.ko: 굳이 속마음을 노골화할 필요까지는 없었다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think there was no need to lay my true feelings out so openly.

explain: 숨기던 생각이나 태도를 겉으로 드러낸다는 점에서 '드러내다'와 비슷하지만, 보통 좋지 않은 의도나 갈등에 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나오는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '노골적으로 말하다', '대놓고 말하다'처럼 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It is like '드러내다' (to reveal) in showing what was hidden, but it usually applies to bad intentions or conflicts. It is a stiff word common in news and writing. In everyday talk people say '노골적으로 말하다' or '대놓고 말하다' instead.

examples.en: Ducks are swimming around leisurely in the pond.

examples.ko: 주말에는 산과 계곡을 노닐며 쉬고 싶어요.
examples.en: On weekends I want to rest, wandering through mountains and valleys.

examples.ko: 시인은 자연 속에서 노니는 삶을 꿈꿨어요.
examples.en: The poet dreamed of a life of roaming freely in nature.
The children played around in the flower garden and then went home.
I miss the days when I used to stroll along the river.
Fish are swimming about in the clear water.

explain: '놀다'와 달리 한가롭게 여기저기를 거닐며 즐기는 모습을 그리는 말이라 글이나 시에서 자주 보여요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '노니는, 노니까'처럼 바뀌어요. 보통 말할 때는 '산책하다'나 '놀다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '놀다', it paints a picture of wandering about at ease and enjoying yourself, so you often see it in writing and poems. The 'ㄹ' drops, giving forms like '노니는' and '노니까'. In everyday speech people usually say '산책하다' or '놀다'.

examples.ko: 그 광산에서 금이 나와서 노다지를 캤대요.
examples.en: They say gold came out of that mine and they struck it rich.

examples.ko: 노다지를 찾겠다고 산속을 헤맨 사람이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people wandered the mountains hoping to find a bonanza.
This new product became a gold mine for the company.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 장사가 잘돼서 노다지나 다름없어요.
examples.en: That shop does so well that it's practically a gold mine.

examples.ko: 땅을 팠더니 노다지라도 나온 것처럼 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: They dug the ground and were as happy as if they had hit a bonanza.
This information is a goldmine for marketers.

explain: 원래는 금이나 은이 많이 묻힌 광맥을 말하지만, 요즘은 돈이 되는 일이나 분야를 비유할 때도 써요. '대박'은 한 번의 큰 성공에 많이 쓰고, '노다지'는 계속 이익이 나올 것 같은 곳이라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It originally means a rich vein of gold or silver, but today it is also used figuratively for a profitable job or field. '대박' is often a single big success, while '노다지' feels like a source that keeps paying off.

examples.ko: 친구들과 카페에서 노닥거리다 보니 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: I chatted idly with friends at a cafe and time flew by.

examples.ko: 일은 안 하고 노닥거리지 말고 빨리 끝내세요.
examples.en: Stop fooling around chatting and finish up quickly.
My coworkers are chatting away in the break room.
We idled around gossiping during the lunch break.
I got scolded by the teacher for chatting during class.
Do your homework first instead of wasting time chatting.

explain: 별 의미 없는 이야기를 늘어놓는다는 뜻에 '할 일은 안 하고'라는 못마땅한 느낌이 함께 있어서 꾸짖을 때 자주 어울려요. 그냥 편하게 이야기하는 '수다 떨다'보다 더 부정적이에요.
explain_en: It means chatting about nothing in particular, with a disapproving feeling of 'instead of doing what you should', so it often fits a scolding. It is more negative than '수다 떨다', which is just casual chatting.

examples.en: The farmers sang work songs while planting rice.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 옛날 어부들이 부르던 노동요예요.
examples.en: This is a work song that fishermen used to sing long ago.

examples.ko: 노동요를 틀어 놓고 청소하면 힘이 덜 들어요.
examples.en: If you put on some music while cleaning, it feels less tiring.

examples.ko: 요즘은 일할 때 듣는 음악을 노동요라고 불러요.
examples.en: These days people call the music they listen to while working a 'work song'.

examples.ko: 제 노동요 목록에는 빠른 노래가 많아요.
examples.en: My work playlist has a lot of upbeat songs.
Thanks to my work music, even boring dishwashing became fun.

explain: 원래는 일을 하면서 힘을 맞추고 지루함을 덜려고 부르던 민요를 말해요. 요즘은 청소나 공부, 일할 때 기분을 올려 주는 음악을 농담처럼 '노동요'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: Originally it means a folk song sung while working to keep time and ease boredom. Nowadays people also jokingly call any music that lifts their mood while cleaning, studying or working a '노동요'.

examples.en: You can feel the experienced polish in that player's game.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 일 처리에 노련미가 생겨요.
examples.en: The older you get, the more seasoned you become at handling work.

examples.ko: 신입은 패기가 넘치고 선배는 노련미로 승부해요.
examples.en: Newcomers have energy, while seniors win with their experience.

examples.ko: 노련미를 보여 준 감독 덕분에 팀이 이겼어요.
examples.en: The team won thanks to the manager, who showed real experience.

examples.ko: 이 배우는 연기에서 노련미와 깊이를 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This actor shows both polish and depth in his acting.
He's an employee who also has seasoned skill, so I trust him.

explain: '노련하다'가 사람의 솜씨를 말하는 형용사라면 '노련미'는 그 솜씨가 겉으로 풍기는 느낌이에요. '느껴지다, 묻어나다, 돋보이다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '노련하다' describes a person's skill, while '노련미' is the seasoned air that skill gives off. It pairs well with verbs like '느껴지다', '묻어나다' and '돋보이다'.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 노령층도 쓰기 쉽게 만들었어요.
examples.en: This app was made so that even older people can use it easily.
A free course for seniors is being held.

examples.ko: 노령층의 일자리 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The job problems of the elderly often come up in the news.
This area has a high proportion of older residents.
It's a drama that is popular with older viewers.
Among the elderly, health care is especially important.

explain: '노인'은 한 사람도 가리키지만 '노령층'은 나이 많은 사람들의 집단을 가리켜서 통계나 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요. '고령층'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: '노인' can point to a single person, but '노령층' refers to older people as a group, so it often appears in statistics and policy talk. '고령층' is used with a similar meaning.

examples.en: Our country is aging rapidly.
They say we must prepare for an aging society.
Rural areas lack workers because of an aging population.
We need policies to slow down population aging.
The problem of aging concerns all of us.
Even cities are not free from aging.

explain: 인구에서 나이 든 사람의 비율이 늘어나는 것을 말할 때 써요. '고령화'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 한 사람의 몸이 늙는 것은 '노화'라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: It is used when the share of older people in a population grows. '고령화' is used with the same meaning, while one person's body getting older is called '노화', which is a different word.

examples.en: The bread has baked to a light golden yellow.
Now that it's autumn, the ginkgo leaves are turning yellowish.
The yellowish curry looks delicious.
Fry the egg until it turns a light golden color.
The wallpaper turned yellowish in the sunlight.
I spread soft, pale yellow butter on the bread.

explain: '노랗다'보다 색이 옅고 부드러운 노란빛을 말해요. 빵이나 전처럼 구워진 것, 낙엽이나 종이처럼 색이 변한 것에 잘 어울려요. 구워진 모습은 '노릇노릇'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a paler, softer yellow than '노랗다'. It suits things that are baked, such as bread or jeon, and things whose color has changed, like fallen leaves or paper. The look of well-baked food can also be called '노릇노릇'.

examples.en: Please grill the fish until it's golden brown.
The jeon was fried to a nice golden brown.
The chicken is fried golden and looks delicious.

examples.ko: 노릇노릇 잘 익은 고구마를 반으로 갈랐어요.
examples.en: I split the nicely golden roasted sweet potato in half.
Wait until the outside turns golden brown.
I blew on the golden hotteok and ate it.

explain: 음식이 알맞게 잘 구워져 보기 좋은 색이 된 모습을 말해서 보통 좋은 느낌이에요. '노릇노릇하다'처럼 형용사로도 많이 써요. 너무 탄 것에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It describes food that has baked just right to an appealing color, so it usually carries a positive feeling. It is also often used as the adjective '노릇노릇하다'. It is not used for food that is burnt.

examples.ko: 한복 치마에 노리개를 달면 더 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: A hanbok skirt looks prettier with a norigae attached.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 본 노리개는 색이 정말 고왔어요.
examples.en: The norigae I saw at the museum had really lovely colors.
The norigae sways gently at the hem of the skirt.

examples.ko: 노리개에는 보통 매듭과 장식이 달려 있어요.
examples.en: A norigae usually has knots and decorations attached.
Not only rings, but norigae are also traditional accessories.

examples.ko: 기념품 가게에서 작은 노리개로 선물을 골랐어요.
examples.en: At the souvenir shop I picked a small norigae as a gift.

explain: 한복 저고리나 치마에 다는 전통 장신구를 말해요. 같은 말에 '가지고 노는 물건'이라는 뜻도 있어서, 사람을 '노리개로 삼다'라고 하면 함부로 가지고 논다는 아주 나쁜 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: It refers to the traditional ornament attached to a hanbok jacket or skirt. The same word also means a thing to play with, so saying someone treats a person as a '노리개' has a very bad meaning of toying with them.

examples.en: The lamb has a gamey smell.
To get rid of the gamey smell, add ginger.
This meat is tender with no gamey smell.

examples.ko: 노린내에 민감한 사람은 이 요리를 싫어해요.
examples.en: People who are sensitive to gamey smells dislike this dish.

examples.ko: 염소 고기는 노린내 때문에 호불호가 갈려요.
examples.en: Goat meat divides people because of its gamey smell.

examples.ko: 노린내도 거의 안 나서 먹을 만했어요.
examples.en: It hardly had any gamey smell, so it was good enough to eat.

explain: 양고기나 염소 고기처럼 짐승 고기에서 나는 특유의 냄새예요. 생선이나 날것에서 나는 냄새는 '비린내'라고 해서 구분해요. 요리할 때 '노린내를 잡다'처럼 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is the particular smell of animal meat such as lamb or goat. The smell of fish or raw food is called '비린내', so the two are kept apart. In cooking people say things like '노린내를 잡다' (to get rid of the gamey smell).

examples.en: My father flew into a rage when he saw my report card.
The boss blew up when he found out about the mistake.
It's nothing to get that furious about.
He shouted furiously because the promise was broken.
My mom goes ballistic if I tell a lie.
The customer raged, and the shop was in an uproar.

explain: '화내다'보다 훨씬 세게, 펄펄 뛰며 크게 화내는 모습이에요. 아버지나 사장님 같은 윗사람이 화낼 때 어울리고, 높일 때는 '노발대발하세요/하셨어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '화내다' and describes someone leaping with rage. It fits when a father, a boss or another superior gets angry, and the honorific forms are '노발대발하세요' and '노발대발하셨어요'.

examples.en: I'm having my first child at thirty-eight, so they call it a late pregnancy.

examples.ko: 노산은 건강 관리를 더 신경 써야 해요.
examples.en: If you give birth later in life, you need to pay more attention to your health.
The doctor told me to be careful because of my age for childbirth.

examples.ko: 노산의 위험을 줄이려면 운동이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Exercise helps reduce the risks of late childbirth.
These days there are more mothers giving birth later in life.

examples.ko: 친구는 노산이라서 걱정했지만 건강한 아기를 낳았어요.
examples.en: My friend worried about having a baby later in life, but she gave birth to a healthy baby.

explain: 보통 35세 이상의 나이에 아이를 낳는 것을 말해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이고, 다른 사람에게 함부로 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It generally means giving birth at age 35 or older. It is a word used in hospitals and the news, and saying it carelessly to someone else can be rude.

examples.en: In the old days, mules carried loads.
A mule is born from a horse and a donkey.
I saw an old man leading a mule on a country road.
A story about a mule and a farmer appears in the picture book.

examples.ko: 이 그림에는 노새 한 마리가 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: A mule is drawn in this picture.

examples.ko: 노새에 짐을 가득 싣고 길을 떠났어요.
examples.en: They loaded the mule with baggage and set off on the road.

explain: 당나귀와 헷갈리기 쉽지만 다른 동물이에요. 요즘은 직접 보기 어려워서 옛이야기나 그림, 책에서 주로 만나요.
explain_en: It is easy to mix up with a donkey, but it is a different animal. Today it is hard to see in person, so you mostly meet it in old tales, pictures and books.

examples.ko: 이 놀이공원은 남녀노소 누구나 즐길 수 있는 놀이 기구가 많아요.
examples.en: This amusement park has many rides that anyone, young or old, can enjoy.

examples.ko: 이 메뉴는 남녀노소 선호도가 높아서 단체 주문에 많이 시켜요.
examples.en: This menu item is popular with all ages, so it's often ordered for groups.
Regardless of age, health is the most important thing.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 남녀노소가 다 아는 노래예요.
examples.en: This is a song that everybody, young and old, knows.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 노소 구분 없이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: People in our neighborhood get along regardless of age.

examples.ko: 마을 잔치에서는 노소 할 것 없이 함께 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: At the village festival, young and old danced together.

explain: 거의 '남녀노소'라는 말로 굳어서 써요. '노소'만 쓸 때는 '노소를 막론하고', '노소 구분 없이'처럼 나이와 상관없다는 뜻의 말과 함께 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 축제는 남녀노소 누구나 즐길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This festival can be enjoyed by anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남자, 여자, 늙은이, 젊은이를 나란히 말해서 '모든 사람'이라는 뜻이 돼요. 광고나 안내문, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It lines up men, women, old and young to mean 'everybody'. You often hear it in ads, notices and the news.

explain_en: It is used almost entirely as part of the set phrase '남녀노소'. On its own it appears in phrases that mean 'regardless of age', such as '노소를 막론하고' and '노소 구분 없이'.
